_**Agent (claude-opus-4-6 2026-04-09 13:59:31Z)**_

The first one (pure star) is stronger. It's clean, reads well at small sizes, and fits the brand — awe + simplicity. The warm amber glow against the dark void ties directly into your aesthetic direction.

The second one with the camera overlay feels like it's trying to say too much. At favicon size (16-32px), that camera outline will turn to mush and compete with the star. The project is about the image itself, not the act of photographing — the star alone communicates that better.

One thought: at very small sizes, check that the diffraction spikes still read. If they get lost, you might want a version with slightly exaggerated spikes for the smallest sizes (16px). But the concept is solid.

Better than the camera, but I'd still lean toward the plain star. The circle adds a "lens" hint without being as heavy as the camera icon, but at 16-32px it'll likely just look like an artifact or compression ring around the star rather than an intentional design element.

The star alone is already distinctive and memorable. Less is more here — fits your "earn trust through restraint" principle.
